name: Racine Unified School District
calendarType: Four-quarter district calendar with a four-day 5K opening, grade-band-only closures, junior ACT attendance, a separate Early Learning track, and selected early-release Wednesdays
seoTitle: Racine Unified School District Calendar: RUSD Dates & PDFs
seoDescription: Reviewed RUSD dates, 5K staggered start, K-5-only closures, junior ACT day, weather contingencies, Early Learning calendars, and early-release Wednesdays.
districtFact: Racine Unified identifies itself as Wisconsin's fifth-largest school district. Its calendar is unusually program-specific: 5K opens across four days, some professional-learning and conference closures affect only K-5, grade 11 attends alone on ACT day, and 3K, 4K, PCOC, Early Childhood, and the BEE Center generally follow a separate Early Learning calendar.

about.title: The 5K School Year Opens in Four Steps
about.content: The main calendar does not give 5K students one universal first attendance day. Families attend orientation first, students then attend in two surname groups, and all 5K students come together on the fourth date. Older K-12 students begin on the district's printed first day.

about.title: Early Learning Is a Separate Calendar Track
about.content: RUSD directs 3K, 4K, PCOC, Early Childhood, and BEE Center families to the Early Learning calendar. That track adds Family Engagement closures and its own attendance pattern. Goodland Montessori is the named exception and follows the K-12 district calendar.

about.title: K-5 Closures Do Not Always Close Secondary Schools
about.content: Green dates on the district PDF are no-school dates for K-5 only. Students in grades 6-12 remain in session on those professional-learning or conference dates, so the grade range matters more than the event title.

about.title: Juniors Attend on the ACT Day
about.content: The blue March date is a grade 11 ACT testing day. Grades K-10 and 12 do not attend because of professional learning, making it the opposite of a typical all-student testing closure.

about.title: Most Wednesdays Change in 2026-27
about.content: RUSD introduced one-hour early release on 25 selected Wednesdays for educator professional learning communities. The district added six minutes to regular school days, adjusted bus schedules, and published K-5 Extended Learning and middle-school activity arrangements for the transition.

about.title: A Multi-Model Racine County District
about.content: RUSD's official directory spans an early learning center, elementary and K-8 campuses, comprehensive and choice high schools, community schools, Montessori, fine arts, STEAM, International Baccalaureate, dual-language, alternative, and virtual options.

calendarNotes: RUSD calendars require families to identify both grade and program before using a date. The main K-12 calendar uses a four-step 5K start with orientation, two surname cohorts, and the first all-5K day. Green closures apply only to K-5 while grades 6-12 attend; red closures apply to all students. The March ACT date brings grade 11 to school while K-10 and grade 12 stay home. A separate Early Learning PDF controls 3K, 4K, PCOC, Early Childhood, and the BEE Center, including extra Family Engagement days. Goodland Montessori is the explicit exception and follows the K-12 district calendar. Asterisks identify dates that may shift for inclement weather, including a break day and the year-end record or makeup sequence. Beginning in 2026-27, selected Wednesdays release one hour early and require school-specific dismissal-time planning.

planningTips.title: Planning with the RUSD Calendar
content: Choose the student's track first: K-12 main calendar, Early Learning calendar, or Goodland Montessori's stated K-12 exception.
For 5K, use the surname cohort on the PDF rather than treating the district's first day as a normal full-class day.
Read every green date by grade band. K-5 students are out, but grades 6-12 remain in session.
On the blue ACT date, plan for grade 11 attendance only; K-10 and grade 12 do not attend.
In 2026-27, use the school start/end-times page for the bracketed early-release dismissal time; the date list alone does not tell families when each school releases.
Keep asterisked contingent-weather dates flexible because RUSD says they may be adjusted after inclement weather.
Use school communications for graduation, activities, emergency updates, and program details beyond the printable attendance calendar.

livingHere.intro: RUSD serves Racine and surrounding Racine County communities through school models that range from neighborhood elementary campuses to Montessori, IB, arts, engineering, career academies, early learning, and virtual education.

highlights.label: Wisconsin's fifth-largest district
highlights.detail: RUSD uses this description in its official school directory.

highlights.label: 1 early learning center
highlights.detail: Bull Early Education Center specializes in developmentally appropriate programming for three- and four-year-olds.

highlights.label: 5 elementary and 9 K-8 campuses
highlights.detail: The K-8 structure helps explain why the calendar distinguishes K-5 closures from grades 6-12 attendance.

highlights.label: 3 comprehensive high schools
highlights.detail: Case, Horlick, and Park anchor the Academies of Racine career-pathway model.

highlights.label: 2 choice schools serving grades 6-12
highlights.detail: The R.E.A.L. School centers engineering, arts, and leadership, while Walden III offers another choice pathway.

highlights.label: 3K, 4K and 5K pathways
highlights.detail: RUSD offers early-learning options that include full-day, half-day, and dual-language formats at selected locations.

districtFaqs.q: Do all RUSD students start school on the same day?
districtFaqs.a: No. The main calendar gives 5K a staggered opening with family orientation, two surname cohorts, and a later all-5K day. Early Learning programs use a separate staggered calendar.

districtFaqs.q: Which RUSD students use the Early Learning calendar?
districtFaqs.a: RUSD directs 3K, 4K, PCOC, Early Childhood, and BEE Center families to the Early Learning calendar. Goodland Montessori is the stated exception and follows the K-12 district calendar.

districtFaqs.q: What does a green date mean on the RUSD calendar?
districtFaqs.a: Green means no school for K-5 because of professional learning or parent-teacher conferences. Grades 6-12 remain in session.

districtFaqs.q: Who attends school on the RUSD ACT day?
districtFaqs.a: Grade 11 attends for the ACT. Students in K-10 and grade 12 do not attend because the date is also used for professional learning.

districtFaqs.q: How early do RUSD students leave on early-release Wednesdays?
districtFaqs.a: In 2026-27, participating schools release one hour early on the listed Wednesdays. Exact regular and bracketed early-release times vary by school and program on the official start/end-times page.

districtFaqs.q: Are RUSD weather-contingency dates guaranteed no-school days?
districtFaqs.a: No. The asterisk says those dates may be adjusted due to inclement weather. Families should confirm any activation or calendar revision with RUSD.

districtFaqs.q: Is the RUSD calendar available in Spanish?
districtFaqs.a: Yes. RUSD publishes Spanish editions of the main school-year calendar and the Early Learning calendar.

customSections.label: Choose the Correct RUSD Calendar Track
customSections.content: The student's program determines which PDF controls attendance. Goodland Montessori is a narrow but important exception to the general Early Learning rule.

rows: Explicit exception printed on the Early Learning PDF

customSections.label: Three Symbols, Three Attendance Rules
customSections.content: RUSD's colored symbols encode grade-level attendance rather than decoration.

customSections.label: Why One District Calendar Still Needs School-Level Follow-up
customSections.content: RUSD's campuses include half-day and full-day 4K, dual-language programs, Montessori, K-8 schools, comprehensive and choice high schools, alternative learning, and virtual coursework. The district PDF establishes the attendance baseline, while bell times, program sessions, activities, and graduation details remain school- or program-specific.
